test_title: SSC Steno 2021 Official Paper (Held on: 12 Nov 2021 Shift 1
subject: general
question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution provides for the disqualification of a member of either House of Parliament for holding any ‘office of profit’ under the Government of India?
solution:
The correct answer is **102.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​(1) According to **Article 102 **of The Constitution of India (1949), a person is ineligible to be elected to and to serve in either House of Parliament if they **meet the following criteria:**

 
 
• **​**(a) They hold a profit-making position with the **Government of India or with the Government of any State**, unless that position has been specifically exempted by law passed by Parliament; 
 
• (b) They are **mentally ill **and have been so determined by a competent court;
 
• (c) They are undischarged** insolvent. **
 
• (d) If he is otherwise ineligible under any law passed** **by the Parliament. A person is not considered to occupy a **profit- making **position under the governments of India or any State for the purposes of this section just because he serves as a minister for either the** Union or that State.**
 
 
 
• 
 
(2) If a **person is so disqualified** under the Tenth Schedule, they are unable to serve as a member of either **House of Parliament.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 The Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies' 10-year time limit for getting rid of the seats reserved for people from Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes has been extended by the 104th Amendment to the Indian Constitution.
 
 
• 
 **ARTICLE 98**-​ (1) There must be a separate secretarial staff for each House of Parliament. The establishment of positions that are shared by the two Houses of Parliament is not prohibited by anything in this section, nevertheless.
 
 
• 
 (2) The conditions of employment for individuals hired to the secretarial staff of either House of Parliament may be regulated by law.
 
 
• 
 (3) The President may, after consulting with the Speaker of the House of People or the Chairman of the Council of States, as applicable, make rules governing the hiring of individuals and the terms of their employment on the secretarial staff of the House of People or the Council of States.
